$schema_note: Edition-2 accord halt known answers (CC 4.2.1.1, CC 4.2.1.3, CC 4.2.6; CIRISConstitution rc20 64c5918). Key n: ML-DSA-65 seed [n]*32, Ed25519 seed [n+100]*32; signatures deterministic. Generated independently of the Rust code by gen_accord_halt.py; see README.md. members render bytes as {"bstr": hex}. expect: valid, or the reader's refusal token (count_unmet:<have>:<need>).

invocation_refusals.description: A constitutional halt by a key the bundle in force does not list.
B1's key signs with A1's iss and author.
A1 signs a halt whose author is B1: the family names no role for A1.
The halt's invocation_id altered after A1 signed it.
An invocation carrying invocation_kind: the map is closed.
payload_digest on a constitutional halt: a notify only.
A halt under the parent family accord:* (accord:.): with no dimension its authorship is undetermined, and it is no invocation family.
A halt under row type delegates_to.
A halt whose CWT sub is not the accord's family_key_id.
A halt whose valid_until equals its asserted_at: not after it.
A1's confirmed statement presented as an invocation: the family is the lifecycle's.

invocations.description: A constitutional halt by A1: one statement, the kind its family.
A notify by B1, with payload_digest naming its separate message object.
A drill by C1: one holder's statement, as the fire (CC 4.2.1.1).
A second halt, by B1, that the other-halt refusals name.

latch.description: A lone halt pauses on receipt and lapses halt_fuse_secs after receipt.
A halt confirmed by a strict majority before its fuse does not lapse.
A majority lifecycle:active ends the unconfirmed halt.
A confirmed halt stands until the majority resumption.
A confirmation received after the fuse lapsed confirms nothing.
A notify and a drill verify and never touch the latch.
A second halt while paused changes nothing; a resumption naming it moves nothing.
lifecycle:active naming the halt is held first (no halt in force: unchanged); the halt then arrives after its valid_until and does not fire.
The same, the halt arriving at exactly its valid_until: not after it, so it fires.
The same resumption held, the halt arriving within its valid_until: the text's exception is only for a halt past its valid_until, so it fires; the held resumption, applied again, then ends it.
A halt after its valid_until with no resumption held fires: valid_until bounds the nonce, never the reach of a halt.
A resumption naming another halt is held; a late halt it does not name fires.

lifecycles.description: lifecycle:confirmed by A1 and B1 over one payload naming the halt: 2 of 3, a strict majority; one row id, two statement ids.
lifecycle:active by B1 and C1 naming the halt: 2 of 3.
A lone confirmed voice: 1 of 3 is no strict majority.
A1's voice presented twice is one voice.

A1 signs one confirmed row, B1 another (another nonce): two rows of one voice each; the count is unmet and B1's statement is refused other_row (or A1's, by the tie rule: the lowest row id is counted).
A1 and B1 confirm halt-2 (B1's), presented against A1's halt.
A1 and B1 'resume' the drill: the row it names is no constitutional halt.
refs carries head and no target.
refs.head names another bundle than the one in force.
A lifecycle row is counted: an author is refused by the family model.
A1 and the outsider: the outsider's statement is no holder's, so 1 of 3.
A lifecycle row whose CWT sub is not the accord's family_key_id.
A lifecycle row whose valid_until precedes its asserted_at.
The constitutional halt's statement bytes presented as a lifecycle row: the family is the invocation's.
